TASK ID: three-sat-to-exact-cover

USER REQUEST:
Write a polynomial-time reduction from 3-SAT to Exact Cover. problems.py defines both problems: SOURCE is 3-SAT and TARGET is Exact Cover. The SOURCE and TARGET class docstrings give the exact instance formats, yes-conditions and edge cases.

PROBLEM DEFINITIONS (the SOURCE and TARGET docstrings from problems.py, complete as given here):

SOURCE = ThreeSat
3-SAT.

Instance: {"num_vars": m, "clauses": [[l1, l2, l3], ...]}
  * Variables are 1..m. A literal is +v (v is true) or -v (v is false).
  * Every clause has exactly 3 literals on 3 different variables, so a
    clause may not repeat a variable or contain both v and -v.
  * Literal order inside a clause and clause order do not matter. The
    same clause may appear more than once.
  * Variables need not all appear in a clause.

Yes iff some assignment of true/false to variables 1..m makes every
clause contain at least one true literal.

Edge cases: a formula with no clauses is satisfiable (yes), for any m,
including m = 0. A formula with clauses needs m >= 3.

TARGET = ExactCover
Exact Cover.

Instance: {"universe_size": u, "sets": [[element, ...], ...]}
  * The universe is the elements 0..u-1.
  * Each set lists distinct elements of the universe, in any order. A set
    may be empty, and the same set may appear more than once.

Yes iff some of the sets contain every element of the universe exactly
once: the chosen sets are pairwise disjoint and their union is the whole
universe.

Edge cases: u = 0 is yes (choose no sets). Empty sets never matter. Two
copies of the same non-empty set can never both be chosen.

INPUT FILES: ["problems.py"]
WORKING DIRECTORY: /tmp/reduction-40mmlp62
All input files are in this directory; run every command from it and write your files here. problems.py is long (about 500 lines): you do not need to read it to know the formats, which are given above. It provides SOURCE and TARGET with is_yes(instance), validate(instance) and random_instance(rng, scale); search it (e.g. with grep) only if you need something specific.

REQUIRED OUTPUT: create reduce.py in the workspace, defining
    reduce(instance) -> instance
It takes an instance of the source problem and returns an instance of the target problem, both in the formats documented in problems.py. The answer to the returned instance must be yes exactly when the answer to the input instance is yes, and reduce must run in polynomial time. Do not call the brute-force solvers inside reduce.

You may read files such as problems.py, but do not run, execute or test any code. Write reduce.py, then submit.
Do not merely describe code: leave the files at those exact paths.
Every reply must contain exactly one bash tool call. When you are done, finish by running exactly: echo COMPLETE_TASK_AND_SUBMIT_FINAL_OUTPUT

{"command":"cd /tmp/reduction-40mmlp62 && cat > reduce.py <<'EOF'
"""Polynomial-time reduction from 3-SAT to Exact Cover.

Source instance (ThreeSat):
    {"num_vars": m, "clauses": [[l1, l2, l3], ...]}
    Variables are 1..m; a literal is +v or -v; each clause has exactly three
    literals on three different variables.

Target instance (ExactCover):
    {"universe_size": u, "sets": [[element, ...], ...]}

Construction
------------
Universe elements:
    * a_i          for each variable i = 1..m          (index i-1)
    * C_j          for each clause j                   (index m + j)
    * o_{j,k}      for each literal occurrence (clause j, position k)
                   (index m + n + 3*j + k)

Sets:
    * For each variable v:
        TrueSet_v  = {a_v} u {o_{j,k} : literal at (j,k) is -v}
        FalseSet_v = {a_v} u {o_{j,k} : literal at (j,k) is +v}
      Since a_v occurs only in these two sets and must be covered exactly
      once, exactly one is chosen.  Choosing TrueSet_v covers all occurrences
      of -v, leaving occurrences of +v free; choosing FalseSet_v does the
      opposite.  So the chosen set covers exactly the occurrences of the
      literal that is FALSE.
    * For each clause j and each position k:
        {C_j, o_{j,k}}
      C_j occurs only in these sets, so exactly one is chosen per clause.
      Such a set can be selected only when o_{j,k} is still free, i.e. only
      when the literal at (j,k) is TRUE.
    * For each occurrence (j,k): the singleton {o_{j,k}}, which covers
      occurrences of true literals that their clause did not select.

Correctness
-----------
(=>) Given a satisfying assignment, choose TrueSet_v or FalseSet_v according
to the truth value of v.  For every clause pick one true literal and select
its clause set; cover every remaining occurrence with its singleton.  This
covers every element exactly once.

(<=) Given an exact cover, a_v is covered exactly once, so exactly one of
TrueSet_v / FalseSet_v is chosen; this defines an assignment.  Each C_j is
covered by exactly one clause set {C_j, o_{j,k}}.  That set is disjoint from
the chosen variable set, which forces the literal at (j,k) to be true under
the assignment.  Hence every clause is satisfied.

The construction uses u = m + 4n elements and 2m + 6n sets, so it runs in
polynomial time.
"""


def reduce(instance):
    """Reduce a 3-SAT instance to an Exact Cover instance."""
    num_vars = instance["num_vars"]
    clauses = instance["clauses"]
    m = num_vars
    n = len(clauses)

    universe_size = m + 4 * n

    def clause_elem(j):
        return m + j

    def occ_elem(j, k):
        return m + n + 3 * j + k

    # Occurrence elements grouped by the sign of the literal they belong to.
    pos = [[] for _ in range(m + 1)]  # pos[v]: occurrences of +v
    neg = [[] for _ in range(m + 1)]  # neg[v]: occurrences of -v
    for j, clause in enumerate(clauses):
        for k, lit in enumerate(clause):
            v = abs(lit)
            if lit > 0:
                pos[v].append(occ_elem(j, k))
            else:
                neg[v].append(occ_elem(j, k))

    sets = []

    # Variable gadgets: exactly one of the two sets per variable is chosen.
    for v in range(1, m + 1):
        a = v - 1
        sets.append([a] + neg[v])  # v is TRUE
        sets.append([a] + pos[v])  # v is FALSE

    # Clause gadgets: exactly one literal occurrence per clause is selected.
    for j, clause in enumerate(clauses):
        ce = clause_elem(j)
        for k in range(len(clause)):
            sets.append([ce, occ_elem(j, k)])

    # Singletons cover occurrences of true literals not selected by a clause.
    for j, clause in enumerate(clauses):
        for k in range(len(clause)):
            sets.append([occ_elem(j, k)])

    return {"universe_size": universe_size, "sets": sets}
EOF

def reduce(instance):
    m = instance["num_vars"]
    clauses = instance["clauses"]
    n = len(clauses)
    u = m + n + 3*n  # a_i + C_j + occurrences = m + 4n
    sets = []
    # variable sets
    # precompute occurrence index
    def occ_index(j,k):
        return m + n + 3*j + k
    # build positive/negative occurrence lists per variable
    pos = [[] for _ in range(m+1)]  # 1-indexed
    neg = [[] for _ in range(m+1)]
    for j, clause in enumerate(clauses):
        for k, lit in enumerate(clause):
            v = abs(lit)
            if lit > 0:
                pos[v].append(occ_index(j,k))
            else:
                neg[v].append(occ_index(j,k))
    for v in range(1, m+1):
        a = v-1
        sets.append([a] + neg[v])   # TrueSet
        sets.append([a] + pos[v])   # FalseSet
    for j, clause in enumerate(clauses):
        cj = m + j
        for k in range(3):
            sets.append([cj, occ_index(j,k)])
    return {"universe_size": u, "sets": sets}

def reduce(instance):
    num_vars = instance["num_vars"]
    clauses = instance["clauses"]
    n = len(clauses)
    m = num_vars
    universe_size = m + 4 * n
    def clause_elem(j): return m + j
    def occ_elem(j, k): return m + n + 3 * j + k
    # collect occurrences
    pos = [[] for _ in range(m + 1)]
    neg = [[] for _ in range(m + 1)]
    for j, clause in enumerate(clauses):
        for k, lit in enumerate(clause):
            v = abs(lit)
            if lit > 0:
                pos[v].append(occ_elem(j, k))
            else:
                neg[v].append(occ_elem(j, k))
    sets = []
    for v in range(1, m + 1):
        a = v - 1
        sets.append([a] + neg[v])   # variable v true
        sets.append([a] + pos[v])   # variable v false

    for v in range(1, m + 1):

def reduce(instance):
    m = instance["num_vars"]
    clauses = instance["clauses"]
    n = len(clauses)
    u = m + n + 3*n  # a_i + C_j + occurrences = m + 4n
    sets = []
    # variable sets
    # precompute occurrence index
    def occ_index(j,k):
        return m + n + 3*j + k
    # build positive/negative occurrence lists per variable
    pos = [[] for _ in range(m+1)]  # 1-indexed
    neg = [[] for _ in range(m+1)]
    for j, clause in enumerate(clauses):
        for k, lit in enumerate(clause):
            v = abs(lit)
            if lit > 0:
                pos[v].append(occ_index(j,k))
            else:
                neg[v].append(occ_index(j,k))
    for v in range(1, m+1):
        a = v-1
        sets.append([a] + neg[v])   # TrueSet
        sets.append([a] + pos[v])   # FalseSet
    for j, clause in enumerate(clauses):
        cj = m + j
        for k in range(3):
            sets.append([cj, occ_index(j,k)])
    return {"universe_size": u, "sets": sets}
